class_guess: Shift-overflow bouncer counter: SOBCv6 TM3's table started in TM3's B; halts after 194 cycles
summary: SOBCv6 TM3's table from TM3's B: 194 shift-overflow cycles, then a far-end carry halts it (tower ~195).
mechanism: Same table as SOBCv6.v TM3 (ours A,B,C,D,E,F = TM3 B,C,A,E,D,F), blank start = TM3 started in B. Left = binary counter of words 001/111 (W0 separator, W1 b = digit b, LSB at the head); right = RC n = 1 (011)^n 01. TM3's proved rules apply verbatim: Incs fills the counter while RC grows by the fill count c; Ov turns RC(2m+2) into m new zero digits and re-reads the old counter with a shift (LOv).

From blank the chain starts at step 847 (x = 1000111011): counts 5, 51, 1,308,622,847, then each count is about 2 to the previous one (shift overflow). Near the head the list freezes into segments between huge (10)^k blocks; the far tail (100-200 symbols) keeps changing.

In the 195th overflow (cycle 194) LOv must increment 0^11 11 11 11 at the far end: the carry runs off the tape and the machine halts (F reads 1). Direct sims of the instantiated tape halt 64 cells from the far end for every block size tried; no earlier cycle hits any failure case.

template.diff: same table after renaming (ours A,B,C,D,E,F = TM3 B,C,A,E,D,F); only the start state differs
template.note: All of TM3's rule lemmas carry over (rename E->D, B->A). New: init (blank -> P x at step 847), 194 step_recs instead of 2, LInc_rec through (10) blocks with a lower bound, explicit pairs on the far side of abstract blocks (TM3's layout breaks at our cycle 4), and a far-end 'overflow halts' predicate instead of TM3's near-head direct run.

strategy: HALT proof from TM3's module: new init by solve_init to step 847, a lower-bounded block representation, 194 step_recs by vm_compute, then an inductive 'overflow halts' predicate (deep part halts => whole halts) with a far-end base case.
risks: 194 vm_compute step_recs on lists up to ~38.5k items may be slow; fallback: compress the frozen near-head segments.
The block representation must carry lower bounds (k >= 2) for LInc through (10) blocks; get the layout wrong and LOv_rec fails as TM3's did at our cycle 4.
The final halt needs a new predicate over the whole counter (~190 abstract blocks); TM3's near-head step1 tail does not reach the far end.
